1583@Person@P_024339@@@@@@@@@26.0@12.0@Beratzhausen, Diocese of Regensburg, Germany@1883.0@@@@@維@Wei@昌祿@Changlu@@@Catholic@@@@@@3@10.0@@1941.0@@1908@@@@@@Weig@@Male@@Georg@@@@@@@@@@Germany@From 1907–1908 Georg Weig studied Canon Law in Rome and received a Ph.D. there. Soon after his arrival in South Shandong, he worked as a teacher for Dogmatics and Apologetics and educator at the Yanzhou seminary. In 1912, he became secretary to the bishop → Augustin Henninghaus (1862–1939), from 1915 to 1925 he was director of the Yanzhou seminary. Since 1922 he was also assistant to the regional SVD superior → Hermann Schoppelrey (1876–1940). Weig participated in the synods of Tianjin and Hankou from 1922-1923 and the National council in Shanghai in 1924. In 1925, he became rector of the SVD house in Yanzhou. Despite having no field experience as a missionary, Weig was made Apostolic prefect of Qingdao. Three years later, in 1928, Weig was elevated to the rank of Apostolic vicar of the Qingdao vicariate and bishop of Qingdao. From the end of 1929 till May 1930 Weig traveled to Europe and the USA. In 1932 he invited the first Sister-Servants of the Holy Spirit of Perpetual Adoration (SSpSAP) to Qingdao to found their convent in China. In 1934 he consecrated the cathedral of Qingdao, the building of which he had started in 1931. From 1935-1936, Weig made another trip to Germany, Rome, and the USA. He died in Qingdao in on 3 October 1941 after an operation of stomach ulcer and was buried in the cathedral. Georg Weig was related to several other members of the Arnoldian family: He was a nephew of Fr. → Johann Baptist Anzer(1851–1903), the brother of Fr. → Karl Weig (1876–1939) and Br. Hugo (Johann) Weig SVD (1890–1972) and the SSpS sisters → Luca (Katharina) Weig (1880–1953) and → Hildeberta (Anna) Weig (1885–1971), as well as a cousin to Fr. → Johann Baptist Weig (1867–1948). He published the annual reports from Qingdao diocese in the Steyler Missionsbote from 1925/1926 until 1940/1941 and the Manuale in usum Missionarorum (Qingdao 1930), which comprised canonical rules for all important aspects of the Church life in the Apostolic Vicariate Yanzhou. Another focus of Georg Weig was the teaching of Latin on which he published among others the following titles: Ladingwen chuxue huagui 拉丁文初学话规. Rudimenta linguae Latinae Grammatica (Qingdao 1932, first edition 1915), Ladingwen chuxue keben 拉丁文初学课本. Rudimenta linguae Latinae Exercitia (Qingdao 1937), and Lading cilin 拉丁辞林. Tian Gengxin was baptized in 1901, his father was a convert. In 1904, Tian Gengxin entered the Minor Seminary in Yanzhoufu where he was ordained as a priest in 1918. Before entering the SVD in 1929, he worked as a pastor in Shandong, in particular Shanxian, Juye, Zhucheng, and Fanxian. From 1929 till 1931, he spent his novitiate in Daijia. He rose quickly in the Catholic hierarchy and at the end of 1945, he was the first Chinese as well as the first Asian to be made cardinal. He joined the Sacred college of cardinals on 18 February 1946. In fall 1948, he was in Shanghai for treatment of a severe illness of his eyes. In December 1948, he was in Hong Kong, initially for a temporary stay. However, he was unable to return to his bishop’s see in Beijing and stayed in exile in Hong Kong until 1951 and then in the USA until 1959. On 16 December 1959 he was made Apostolic administrator of the archdiocese of Taipei and moved to Taiwan in 1960. Tian Gengxin was a member of the papal conclaves of 1958 and 1963, the Missions Commission, as well as a member of the preparatory commission to the Second Vatican Council (1962–1965) in which he also participated.
